comment: Menu art drawn as glyphs in the inventory TITLE. A title glyph renders behind the items and
in front of the container background, which is exactly the layer a menu backdrop needs.
U+E901  garden_shop_gui.png       the sell menu: three drawn shelves in the panel
U+E902  garden_shop_gui_list.png  the price book: the same stand with the panel left empty
Both are a 256x256 canvas whose art occupies x 2..253, y 0..238, and both render 1:1 at
height:256. That the scale is 1:1 is measured, not assumed: the slot cells drawn in the art
are 18 px apart, the vanilla pitch, so any scaling would put items off-centre in the very
cells drawn for them.
ascent:29, and background-x-offset:-47 in gui.yml, come from that same measurement:
drawn columns  x 47, 65, 83 ... 191    vanilla slots start at x 8    -> shift left 39
drawn rows     y 156, 174, 192, 214    vanilla player rows 140, 158, 176, 198 -> up 16
A glyph's top row lands at baseline - ascent and the title baseline is y=13, so putting
the canvas top at y=-16 needs ascent = 13 + 16 = 29. The title cursor starts at x=8, so
putting the canvas left edge at x=-39 needs an offset of -47.
The awning therefore overhangs the window by 16 px above and the stand by ~37 px each side,
which is how it was drawn: the window's bottom edge lands exactly on the art's.
U+E9B0..U+E9B7  positive advances  +1 +2 +4 +8 +16 +32 +64 +128
U+E9B8..U+E9BF  negative advances  -1 -2 -4 -8 -16 -32 -64 -128
Binary building blocks: any pixel offset is a short combination of these. The plugin
composes them in MenuBackground, so the X position is tunable from gui.yml without
touching this file.
Escapes, not literal characters: a private-use codepoint written raw is invisible in every
editor and does not survive an encoding round-trip.
To move the art vertically or rescale it, change ascent/height below, then run
./gradlew packZip
which rebuilds the zip and recomputes its SHA-1. Horizontal moves need no rebuild.
